homeTitle: seine — the fastest Blocknet miner for CPU, NVIDIA and AMD GPU
homeDescription: seine is the fastest miner for Blocknet, the Argon2id privacy coin. Tuned kernels for modern CPUs, NVIDIA GPUs and AMD Radeon GPUs, zero configuration, free and open source.
heroLead: Mines Blocknet on any modern CPU, NVIDIA GPU or AMD Radeon GPU, and picks the fastest settings for your machine on its own. Free and open source.
step1Text: Each CPU thread uses about 2 GB of RAM. Seine sizes itself to your machine.
step2TextHtml: Double-click seine.exe on Windows. On macOS or Linux:
step3TextHtml: Or your @shortname. Accept the default pool and you're mining; seine keeps tuning itself as it runs.
dashboardAlt: The seine dashboard mining on bntpool from an Apple M4 Max at 30.6 H/s
perfSub: Seine tests its kernels on your machine while it mines and keeps the fastest one.
feat1Text: Separate Argon2id kernels for AVX2, AVX-512, Arm NEON and SHA3, plus NVIDIA and AMD Radeon GPUs.
feat2Text: Thread count, CPU kernel, memory and core placement are tested while you mine, with no restarts.
feat3Text: Every core and every NVIDIA and AMD GPU mines at once, and their hashrates add up.
feat4Text: Mines on bntpool.com out of the box, works with any Stratum pool, or solo against your own Blocknet node.
feat5Text: NUMA-aware placement, huge pages, a local control API with live events, and Prometheus metrics.
feat6Text: BSD-3 licensed, with checksums for every release archive.

trackBody: Use the same wallet address or shortname as in Seine. Accepted shares show the pool is receiving your work. The pool’s hashrate estimate can take a few minutes to appear.

msIntroMacHtml: Seine mines on your Mac's CPU and picks the thread count for you. To set your own, close seine and run this from its folder:
msThreadsHtml: Each CPU thread uses about 2 GB of RAM. While seine is running, press - or + to try a different thread count, then use the number you like in the command. Press q to stop mining.
msMoreHtml: These settings last until you close seine. The settings guide shows how to keep them for every start, choose one graphics card, and change your address or pool.
msSlowHtml: Your computer feels slow. Use fewer threads, or press q to stop seine while you need the whole machine.
msLowHtml: Hashrate looks low at first. Seine tunes itself during the first minutes, so give it time before changing anything.
msGpuHtml: A graphics card is missing. Install its current driver and restart seine. See the NVIDIA guide or the AMD guide.
msRamHtml: Seine says it needs more RAM. Use a lower number with --threads, about one thread for every 2 GB of free RAM.
msSavedHtml: Seine asks for your address again. Start it from the same folder as before, because your settings are saved in seine-data there.
msPoolHtml: The pool shows nothing yet. Wait for Accepted to rise in the dashboard, then enter the same address on My Stats. The pool checklist covers the rest.
msBlockedHtml: Windows blocks the download or the app. Follow the download check guide to confirm you have the official file.
